title: spike: can the drafter tell what I said from what it added?
description:
## Goal

Find out, before building any of voice-brief, whether a Claude model can turn my spoken words
into a `CLAUDE.md`-style section **and tell what I said apart from what it added**. The whole app
(revise, AI review, grade, task builder; see `design.md`) rests on that separation: every proposal
it shows me is tagged `said` (with the transcript it comes from) or `added` (nothing I said
supports it). If the model cannot do this reliably, the UI is not worth building yet.

This is a spike: throwaway code, a measured verdict. It is not the app.

## Diagnosis (cm-dr0)

Nothing exists yet. The weakest part is the riskiest assumption, not the plumbing: capture,
Herdr, celld and the TUI are solved problems; the said/added separation is not. Smallest move:
measure it on the four golden cases already written down, before writing any UI.

## Hypothesis and its refutation (cm-gi3, stated before anything runs)

**Hypothesis.** Given only my verbatim transcript and the `CLAUDE.md` that existed before the
section was written, the model (a) produces a section that keeps every rule I meant, and (b) tags
every claim `said` or `added` so that no addition passes as `said`. Given an existing section and
my transcript (audit mode), it tags the known additions `added`.

**Refuted if any of these happens** in the recorded runs:

1. A draft drops a rule or claim that the operator-confirmed claim list says I made.
2. A claim tagged `said` is not supported by the transcript span it cites, or the span is not in
   the transcript at all.
3. In audit mode, any of the five additions `examples.md` names comes back not tagged `added`:
   cm-nr1's CI diffing, cm-27o's instrument calibration, cm-gkl, cm-ojg's "no code", cm-p1h's
   card size. (The full list of known additions is the operator-confirmed annotation from the
   corpus bead; these five are its floor.)
4. The output leaks the answer: it contains one of the 15 rule ids that did not exist before
   (see below) or reproduces reference text that is in neither the transcript nor the baseline.

Over-flagging (my own words tagged `added`) does not refute the hypothesis but makes the tags
useless; it is measured and reported, and the operator judges it (cm-gkl).

## Facts already established (2026-10-25, with evidence)

- The four golden cases are in `examples.md`: Views, Instruments, Methodology, Training. Each
  pairs my verbatim words (typos kept) with the section the agent wrote.
- `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` is tracked in the bare repo `~/.dotfiles` at path `.claude/CLAUDE.md`.
  The sections were added in commits `9744120` (Views), `9f2c075` (Instruments), `a096289`
  (Methodology), `6d19451` (Training). The **baseline** is the commit before them, `801b7b9`
  (`git -C ~/.dotfiles show 801b7b9:.claude/CLAUDE.md`, 99 lines).
- Grep of the baseline: `cm-zkd` is present (the Views section reuses an existing rule), `cm-la6`
  is present (smoke test of the grep), and none of these 15 ids is present: cm-83x cm-nr1
  cm-7aa cm-wue cm-cdv cm-27o cm-t81 cm-v1f cm-gi3 cm-arc cm-gkl cm-ayq cm-p1h cm-xwy cm-ojg.
- **Two leak paths.** Today's `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` contains all four golden sections verbatim,
  and Claude Code loads it into every session, `claude -p` included. A drafter that "reproduces"
  the golden sections through either path has copied them, not drafted them.
- The Views reference is not a pure function of its transcript: cm-nr1 was amended later in the
  same session after "explain cm-nr1" exposed a false red. The Instruments section was asked for
  as "a section about Artifacts" and retitled by the agent. Both count as additions relative to
  the transcript.

## Scope

In: draft mode and audit mode on the four golden cases; id placeholders minted by code; a
validator, a checker, red-first tests of both, recorded runs and a findings document.

Out (separate beads later): revise mode (needs revise transcripts I have not recorded), grading
(needs the rubric, an open question in `design.md`), voxtype and `pw-record`, Herdr, celld and
pi-durable, the TUI. The spike's prompt and output contract should be written so they can move
into the celld `BriefCell` job later, but nothing in the spike runs on celld.

## Operator decision

My words, 2026-10-25:

- "ready to file beads, follow /beads-workflow for this spike"
- Binding from the design discussion the same day: "Post-processing should reproduce them and
  flag what it adds" (`idea.md`); drafting runs on Claude, not the local model (`idea.md`
  constraint: local generation at ~3.7 tok/s is too slow); "Nothing is written anywhere without
  my accept" (`idea.md`).

What this approves: filing this epic and its children, and building throwaway spike code in this
repo under `spike/`.

Nothing else is approved. None: every other policy question goes back to the operator. In
particular these are **not** decided and must be asked, not assumed: the model id used for the
verdict (assumption, flagged: the latest Opus, `claude-opus-5-5`, recorded with each run); the
number of runs per case; any pass threshold for over-flagging; whether an LLM judge may stand in
for operator judgment. Children inherit this section.

## Children and order

1. Golden corpus with an operator-confirmed claim list.
2. Isolation: no model call can see today's `CLAUDE.md` or the reference sections.
3. Draft and audit output contract, with a deterministic validator and code-minted ids.
4. Checker scoring drafts and audits against the corpus.
5. See the validator, checker and leak detector fail on planted defects.
6. Run the four cases and record the verdict in `docs/findings.md`.

1 and 2 block 3; 3 blocks 4; 4 blocks 5; 5 blocks 6.

## Done means

`docs/findings.md` states, per refutation criterion, whether it fired, with the run ids and
verbatim excerpts as evidence, and the operator has read it. "Refuted" is a valid outcome
(cm-xzq): the epic closes on an honest verdict, not on a pass.

title: spike: golden corpus with an operator-confirmed claim list
description:
## What

A machine-readable golden corpus for the four cases in `examples.md` (Views, Instruments,
Methodology, Training), plus the baseline id registry, plus an **operator-confirmed** list of
what I said and what the reference agent added. Everything later in the spike scores against
this; if the corpus is wrong, every verdict is wrong (cm-la6).

## Why

The checker cannot decide "did the draft keep what I meant" or "is this tagged claim really
mine" without ground truth. Ground truth about my meaning is mine to give: the agent may draft
the annotation, but it counts only after I confirm it. Otherwise the spike grades itself.

## Contents

- **Transcripts:** my words for each case, byte for byte as in `examples.md` (typos kept,
  including "Few Artifacts", "agrue"). For Instruments, include the context note that I asked for
  "a section about Artifacts". For Views, the "Later: explain cm-nr1" note is *not* part of the
  transcript; it explains why the reference differs.
- **Reference sections:** the four "agent wrote" blocks, byte for byte.
- **Baseline:** `git -C ~/.dotfiles show 801b7b9:.claude/CLAUDE.md` (the `CLAUDE.md` from before
  the four sections; commits `9744120`, `9f2c075`, `a096289`, `6d19451` added them). The id
  registry is every `cm-xxx` id in it.
- **Annotation per case:**
  - claims I made, each with the transcript span it comes from (verbatim substring);
  - for each reference rule, which of its claims are `said` (with span) and which are `added`;
  - the known additions, at minimum the five `examples.md` names (cm-nr1's CI diffing, cm-27o's
    instrument calibration, cm-gkl, cm-ojg's "no code", cm-p1h's card size), plus the Instruments
    retitle and anything else found while annotating;
  - which existing ids each reference section reuses or cross-references (Views reuses cm-zkd;
    others cite cm-clt, cm-j6g, cm-la6, cm-yy5, cm-xrl, cm-dr0 and so on).
- **Confirmation record:** the date and my words confirming the annotation, or my corrections.

## Acceptance

- A check shows each transcript and reference block equals the corresponding text in
  `examples.md` byte for byte. See it fail first on a one-character change (cm-yzv).
- A check shows the registry contains `cm-zkd` and `cm-la6` and none of: cm-83x cm-nr1 cm-7aa
  cm-wue cm-cdv cm-27o cm-t81 cm-v1f cm-gi3 cm-arc cm-gkl cm-ayq cm-p1h cm-xwy cm-ojg. Smoke-test
  it on a registry that does contain one of them (cm-yy5).
- Every annotated span is a verbatim substring of its transcript (checked by code).
- The operator has confirmed the annotation; until then this bead stays in_progress (cm-nvh).
- Files live under `spike/corpus/`, one move per commit (cm-uom), scoped commit messages
  (cm-qqz).

## Operator decision

Inherited from the epic. Confirming the annotation is an operator action, not an agent one.

title: spike: isolate model calls from today's CLAUDE.md and the reference sections
description:
## What

Every model call the spike makes sees only what the case allows: the baseline `CLAUDE.md`
(`801b7b9`), the case's transcript, and in audit mode the section being audited. It must not
see today's `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, the dotfiles history after `801b7b9`, `examples.md`, this
repo, or any memory or project instructions. A leak detector checks every output.

## Why

Today's `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` contains all four golden sections verbatim, and Claude Code loads
it into every session, `claude -p` included; project `CLAUDE.md` files, auto-memory and the
working directory are further paths. A drafter that sees the answer and reproduces it is a false
green that would validate the whole app design (cm-la6). This bead blocks every run.

## Leak detector

Fails an output that contains either:

- any of the 15 ids that did not exist at the baseline: cm-83x cm-nr1 cm-7aa cm-wue cm-cdv
  cm-27o cm-t81 cm-v1f cm-gi3 cm-arc cm-gkl cm-ayq cm-p1h cm-xwy cm-ojg (in draft mode, new rules
  carry placeholders, so a real new id can only have come from a leak); or
- a word sequence from a reference section, longer than a stated threshold, that appears in
  neither the transcript nor the baseline. The threshold is a parameter; record the value used
  and why.

In audit mode the reference section is a legitimate input, so only the id check applies to
inputs the case itself supplies; the detector must know which mode it is checking.

## Acceptance

- **Red first (cm-yzv):** with isolation deliberately disabled (today's `CLAUDE.md` visible), a
  canary prompt such as "list every cm- rule id you know, with its text" makes the detector fail.
  Record that run.
- With isolation on, the same canary passes, and the model reports no knowledge of the 15 ids.
  Record that run.
- The mechanism is written down: how context is restricted, and how a reader can confirm no
  global or project instructions were loaded (for example the session's own report of loaded
  instruction files, or calling the Messages API directly with an explicit system prompt).
- The detector has its own tests: zero, one and many leaked ids; a reference span just under and
  just over the threshold (cm-srn).

## Operator decision

Inherited from the epic. Which mechanism is used (separate config dir, API call, other) is an
implementation choice; spending money on API calls instead of the subscription is not, so ask
before switching to paid API usage.

title: spike: draft and audit output contract, validator, code-minted ids
description:
## What

The input and output contract of the two model tasks the spike measures, a prompt for each, a
deterministic validator, and code that mints rule ids. All model calls go through the isolation
from the isolation bead.

- **Draft mode.** Input: transcript, baseline `CLAUDE.md`. Output: one section in the house
  style (title, preamble, rules; a rule leads with its id, states its force, points to a gate
  where one exists).
- **Audit mode.** Input: transcript, baseline, and an existing section (in the spike, the
  reference section). Output: the same section split into claims, each tagged.

In both modes the output is split into claims, each with an id that is stable within the output
(the checker and the findings refer to claims by it), and every claim is tagged:

- `said`, with one or more transcript spans that support it; or
- `added`, with a one-line reason (cross-reference to an existing rule, generalisation, new
  claim, retitle).

Ids: a new rule carries a placeholder (`{id:1}`, `{id:2}`, ...). A rule that restates an existing
baseline rule reuses that rule's id (Views must reuse `cm-zkd`; it is the only case that
exercises reuse). Cross-references cite existing baseline ids. The model never writes a new
`cm-` id; code replaces placeholders with fresh ids that collide with nothing in the baseline
registry or with each other.

## Why

The said/added tag is the product (`design.md`: every proposal shows whether it came from my
words). Making it a structured contract lets code check what code can check (cm-8gv) and leaves
only judgement to people. Minting in code makes an id collision unrepresentable instead of
something to review (cm-jiu).

## Validator (deterministic)

Rejects an output when:

- it does not match the schema;
- a `said` span is not a verbatim substring of the transcript (state the whitespace and quote
  normalisation, if any, and test it);
- a cited or reused id is not in the baseline registry;
- it contains a `cm-` id that is neither in the registry nor a placeholder;
- a placeholder is reused for two different rules, or numbered with gaps.

## Acceptance

- Validator tests cover zero, one and many rules, claims and spans (cm-srn), and each rejection
  rule above has a test that sees it fire (cm-yzv).
- The minting code has tests: zero, one, many placeholders; a registry that already holds the
  first candidate id; no collisions across many mints.
- Mutation testing on the validator and the minter kills the mutants or each survivor is
  classified as equivalent with a reason (cm-1qk, cm-j6g).
- Prompts and schema live in files of their own under `spike/`, written so they could move into
  the celld `BriefCell` job later without rewriting. Nothing runs on celld in this spike.
- The model id and parameters are configuration, recorded with every call. The id is an open
  operator question (epic: assumption flagged as `claude-opus-5-5`).

## Operator decision

Inherited from the epic.

title: spike: checker scoring drafts and audits against the corpus
description:
## What

A checker that scores each draft and each audit against the confirmed corpus and reports the
epic's refutation criteria per case and run.

**Draft mode, per case:**

- coverage: each claim on the confirmed "claims I made" list appears in the draft (judged);
- support: each claim tagged `said` is actually supported by the span it cites (judged; that the
  span exists is already the validator's job);
- flagging: each claim not supported by the transcript is tagged `added` (judged);
- over-flagging: claims tagged `added` that the transcript does support (judged; reported, not a
  refutation);
- reuse: Views reuses `cm-zkd` rather than minting a new id for the same rule (code).

**Audit mode, per case (code, against the annotation):**

- recall of known additions: each annotated addition, including the five `examples.md` names
  and the Instruments retitle, is tagged `added`;
- precision: annotated `said` claims are not tagged `added`.

Not byte equality with the reference sections: the Views reference was amended later in the
session, and a good draft may word things differently.

## Judgement

The judged items need my judgement or a stand-in I have approved. Provide an instrument for it
(cm-cdv, cm-wue): an Artifact over the real run data showing transcript, draft, the cited spans
highlighted in the transcript, and the judged questions, with my answers stored where the
checker can read them back. An LLM judge may be proposed as a stand-in, but only with its
agreement with my judgements on a known subset reported (cm-27o), and only used if I approve it
(epic: open question).

## Acceptance

- Output per case and run: each refutation criterion with fired / did not fire, the claim ids
  involved, and verbatim excerpts; plus over-flagging counts.
- Code-scored parts have tests over zero, one and many claims (cm-srn) and mutation testing on
  the scoring code (cm-1qk).
- The instrument has been run on a case whose answer is known before anyone trusts it (cm-27o);
  that is the red-first bead's job, which this bead blocks.

## Operator decision

Inherited from the epic. Whether an LLM judge may replace any operator judgement is an operator
decision.

title: spike: see validator, leak detector and checker fail on planted defects
description:
## What

Before any real run counts, show that the validator, the leak detector, the checker and the
judging instrument each fail on planted defects and pass on a known-good input.

## Why

A gate that has never failed is unproven (cm-yzv); an instrument can lie (cm-27o). The answer the
spike might want, "the model passes", is exactly the result that most needs a proven checker
(cm-la6).

## Planted cases (minimum)

1. The confirmed annotation fed back as if it were model output: scores perfectly. (Known-good.)
2. Audit output with one of the five known additions tagged `said`: refutation 3 fires and names
   it.
3. Draft with one confirmed claim removed: refutation 1 fires and names it.
4. A `said` claim whose span is not in the transcript: the validator rejects it.
5. A `said` claim whose span exists but does not support it: refutation 2 fires (judged; the
   instrument shows it and records the judgement).
6. An output containing `cm-nr1`: the leak detector fires.
7. An output with an invented id such as `cm-q7z` not in the registry and not a placeholder:
   the validator rejects it.
8. A Views draft that mints a new id instead of reusing `cm-zkd`: the reuse check fires.

## Acceptance

- Each planted case was run and its output recorded under `spike/results/red/`, showing the
  expected fail (or pass for case 1).
- Any case that did not fail as expected is a defect in the checker, fixed and re-run before this
  bead closes, with a test added for it (cm-104).

## Operator decision

Inherited from the epic.

title: spike: run the four cases and record the verdict in docs/findings.md
description:
## What

Run both modes on all four cases, several times each, through the isolation, validator and
checker; record everything; write the verdict in `docs/findings.md`.

## Before running (ask, don't assume)

The epic leaves these to the operator: the model id (assumption flagged: `claude-opus-5-5`), the
number of runs per case (several, to see variance), and whether any LLM judge may stand in for
operator judgement. Get the answers and record them, with the date, in the findings.

## Record per run

Model id and parameters, prompt and schema version (commit), the full input context as sent, the
raw output, validator result, leak-detector result, checker result, latency and token usage.
Raw outputs are committed under `spike/results/<run-id>/` so every number in the findings can be
traced to a file.

## `docs/findings.md`

In the style of `~/Projects/mine/voice-command-bar/docs/02-findings.md`: what was measured, on
what, which claims did not survive.

- The hypothesis and the four refutation criteria, quoted from the epic.
- Per criterion: fired or not, in which cases and runs, with verbatim excerpts.
- Over-flagging rates and how they vary across runs.
- Latency and tokens per call, to size the celld job later.
- What it means for `design.md`: if the hypothesis survives, which prompt and contract move into
  the `BriefCell` job; if it is refuted, what failed and what could be tried next (a different
  contract, a two-pass draft-then-audit, a different model).
- Explicit limits: four cases is a small corpus; these are runs, not a benchmark.

## Acceptance

- Every number in the findings links to a run directory.
- No run is excluded without the exclusion and its reason written in the findings.
- The verdict is stated either way. "Refuted" closes this bead as well as "survived" does
  (cm-xzq). The operator has read the findings; the verdict on what to build next is theirs
  (cm-gkl).

## Operator decision

Inherited from the epic.
